facility.name: Wonder World Daycare & Learning Center (Vip)
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips,Night Care

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Non_Exact match: 3660A JOE BATTLE BLVD, EL PASO, TX, 79938

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: Children's Records are incomplete.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours: Training hours for the year are not complete for most caregivers in the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours (26 TAC §746.901(6))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: Operation did not report the number of employees that left the operation for 2024 by the required due date of 01/15/2025
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Minimum Qualifications Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit (Form 2912): All personnel did not have a copy of the 2nd affidavit in their files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Minimum Qualifications Employees and Caregivers - Affidavit (Form 2912) (26 TAC §746.1105(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours: There was one employee that did not have all their annual training hours for the year 2023 to 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours (26 TAC §746.901(6))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation: An employee did not have their annual training hours completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Orientation (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: Director's annual training certificates were not available to evaluate during this inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: Two caregivers out four personnel records evaluated were missing annual training hours. One caregiver was missing four hours for 02/26/2021 to 02/26/2022.  Second Caregiver was missing eight hours for 09/19/2021 to 09/19/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - installed and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions: Van #8, the only van with a child safety alarm system did not function during this inspection. Driver assisted with the testing of the alarm and was not able to activate the alarm after several attempts. Children will not be transported in this vehicle until the child safety alarm system has been repaired.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - installed and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions (26 TAC §746.5625(b))

occurrences.finding: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely: Transportation vehicle (minibus) front row window safety belt was missing a part that must be inserted into the buckle. Four backside seat rests locking latch were not in proper working order. Pictures were taken and uploaded to digital storage. This minibus will not be used to transport children until it has been repaired.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely (26 TAC §746.5603(c))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: Monthly fire drills were missing for January, February, March, and April of 2022. A fire drill under three minutes was conducted and documented during this inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Vehicle Documentation - date of lease or purchase for each vehicle: Vehicle documentation verifying proof of purchase was not available for review for bus C26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Vehicle Documentation - date of lease or purchase for each vehicle (26 TAC §746.5627)

occurrences.finding: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended: A child was left unattended in a transportation van for approximately 5 minutes  after being overlooked by the caregiver in charge of transporting the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended (26 TAC §746.5605(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: An incident report was not completed for an incident in which a child was left unattended in a transportation van placing him at risk of harm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: A caregiver was neglectful by failing to ensure all children exited the transportation van, resulting in a child being placed at risk of harm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to make a report to Child Care Regulation after becoming aware that a child had been placed at risk while in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During the investigation it was determined a caregiver failed to exercise proper supervision by leaving the toddler classroom unattended several times.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Injuries Requiring Medical Treatment or Hospitalization: The operation failed to generate an incident/illness report for a child that required medical treatment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Injuries Requiring Medical Treatment or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.701(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During the DFPS investigation, it was determined that neglect occurred with a child in care who was seriously injured, resulting from the caregiver's inadequate supervision and conscious disregard for the safety and well-being of the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Children in Control: Based on the video footage obtained through the investigation, children were observed to be out of control, wrestling with one another, hitting each other in the face, and running out of the toddler classroom while a caregiver was on her cell phone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: It was determined that a caregiver failed to use good judgment when she failed to attend to a child's needs after he was injured and exhibited signs of pain and discomfort.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities: During the investigation it was determined a caregiver was using her personal cell phone while caring for children, as a result a child was severely injured.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Operation failed to notify Child Care Regulations in a timely manner of a child who was injured and received medical treatment. Parent notified the operation on 04/08/2022, the operation notified Child Care Regulations after hours by leaving a message on the intake line on 04/11/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022, as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: Former caregiver confirmed she was present at the operation in care of infants on Monday 12/06/2021, Tuesday 12/07/2021, and Wednesday 12/08/2021, Caregiver resigned Wednesday night 12/08/2021. Caregiver was not present during the investigation on 12/13/2021, however CLASS indicated caregiver had a PENDING status. Director, designee, and an infant caregiver acknowledged former infant caregiver's presence at the operation on the above-mentioned dates. Former caregiver eligibility letter was received by the operation on 12/15/2021.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: During the investigation/inspection a six-month-old infant was observed sleeping in a restrictive device (bouncy). Corrected during inspection when infant caregiver moved infant to a crib. (Photo taken).
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426)

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink: During the investigation the handwashing sink in the infant room had a small plastic dish rack with bottles and infant dishes as well as a bottle of liquid dish soap on the side. (Photo taken)
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink (26 TAC §746.2419(8))
